A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe RL3DEdit, with matching core methods, experiments and main results despite the changed title. v1 ends after its references despite referring to an appendix; v2 includes supplementary Sections S1–S5. These support comparison of newly documented material without establishing when the underlying experiments were performed.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-editing comparisons, reward ablations, backbone evaluations and VGGT confidence analysis in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–8.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and additionally reports split-specific scores, user preferences, further ablations and qualitative analyses in its supplement.

M1.justification: The FLUX-Kontext editor, GRPO optimization and four reward components remain unchanged. Section S4.2 adds a limited inference adaptation that duplicates fewer views, exemplified by four, into nine input slots. The newly specified AnySplat initialization and 3DGS refinement otherwise document the previously described reconstruction stage rather than establish its replacement.

E1.justification: The scene-editing datasets and GEdit-Bench-EN evaluation are retained, as are eight training scenes, 70 prompts and the 100-case evaluation partition. Tables S1–S3 identify previously described scenes and instructions. Additional examples and view-count handling remain within the existing editing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DGE, GaussCtrl, EditSplat and EditSplat with FLUX-Kontext; Table S4 reports the same comparator set by split. Table 2 retains the alternative verifiers and Qwen-Image-Edit variant. Section S2.4 explains the existing adapted EditSplat baseline rather than introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: The main split, metrics and default training configuration remain unchanged. Reported training and timing hardware changes from RTX A6000 to RTX Pro 6000, without establishing reruns. Table S5 adds fixed-anchor, 6/20-step and unequal-reward-weight controls within the retained face-scene protocol; S4.2 also describes four-view input handling.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and verifier ablations, Table S5 quantitatively tests anchor selection, denoising-step count and reward-weight balance. Figure S2 adds confidence-map evidence for blurry, distorted and high-quality inputs. These additions substantially expand validation of design choices and verifier behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added user-study percentages also lack uncertainty estimates. VGGT confidence maps and GRPO candidate-group sizes concern the algorithm rather than statistical uncertainty in reported performance.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical entries. Newly supplied Table S4 reports RL3DEdit VIEScores of 5.52/5.40 and user preferences of 71.4%/60.0% for in-distribution/zero-shot cases. Table S5 adds design-variant outcomes, including fixed-anchor VIEScore 4.54 versus random-anchor 5.26. Figures S1–S2 add qualitative evidence; these are additional results, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Sections S2.1–S2.2 supply previously deferred formal definitions, including the flow-to-SDE equation, clipped GRPO surrogate and SfM reward. The main reward equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced. The standard CLIP metric formula is explanatory rather than a theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: RL-based scene editing using VGGT verification, preserved editing quality, generalization, backbone transfer and over 2× speedup. The new title and supporting evidence do not redefine those central claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 and S4.3 newly acknowledge failure under drastic non-rigid deformations such as bowing the head. v2 also explains using VIEScore alongside blur-sensitive Ph-Loss and interprets the added anchor, denoising and reward-weight comparisons. The central explanation of VGGT's resistance to reward hacking is retained.

D1.justification: The supplement supplies substantial missing implementation and evaluation information: AnySplat initialization, 3,000-step 3DGS refinement, adapted EditSplat guidance, metric/reward computation, scene-specific prompt lists and a 25-participant video-preference protocol. These largely document previously referenced procedures. The promise to release code and models remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including AnySplat, standard 3D Gaussian Splatting, InsertNeRF and Thinking with Camera, alongside other background references. The related-work taxonomy, comparisons with existing editing paradigms and claimed first application of RL to 3D editing remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, its running headers change, and localized prose and caption wording are refined. Keywords, acknowledgements and an indexed supplement are added. The main six-section narrative and most existing paragraphs remain intact rather than undergoing extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: Tables S1–S5 and Figures S1–S2 substantially expand visual documentation of instructions, split results, ablations and verifier behavior. Main figures are largely retained, with Figure 6 relocated and some captions and diagram labels revised. The major change comes from the added displays rather than pagination alone.

improvement.justification: v1 defers essential reconstruction, baseline and dataset information to an absent appendix. v2 supplies that material and adds controlled ablations, split-specific results and user preferences, substantially improving reproducibility and empirical support without changing headline scores. The explicit deformation limitation also clarifies applicability. The unexplained GPU revision and continued absence of statistical uncertainty remain weaknesses, but do not outweigh these gains.
